question: Your PostgreSQL query takes 5 seconds in production but runs instantly in development. What do you investigate?
title: Debugging Slow PostgreSQL Queries in Production
direct_answer: First, run EXPLAIN ANALYZE on the exact production query. Common causes of dev/prod performance difference: production has more data (Seq Scan becomes slow), stale statistics (run ANALYZE or check autovacuum), missing index only on dev, different query plan due to data distribution differences, index bloat, or table bloat. Enable pg_stat_statements to see aggregated slow queries. Check pg_stat_user_tables for dead tuples (vacuum needed).
interviewer_intent: Tests production database debugging methodology — structured approach matters more than knowing the answer immediately.

sections.title: Production query debugging workflow
sections.content:
Step 1: Reproduce the slow query. Get the exact query from logs (enable log_min_duration_statement = 1000ms). Run EXPLAIN ANALYZE on the production database.

Step 2: Compare EXPLAIN plans. If dev plan uses Index Scan and prod plan uses Seq Scan: either the index doesn't exist on prod, or the query planner chose differently due to data volume or statistics.

Step 3: Check statistics freshness. Large mismatch between Plan Rows and Actual Rows = stale statistics. Run ANALYZE tablename to update. Check last_analyze in pg_stat_user_tables.

Step 4: Check for table bloat. High dead tuples (from UPDATE/DELETE without vacuum) force sequential scans even with an index. Check pg_stat_user_tables.n_dead_tup. Run VACUUM ANALYZE tablename.

Step 5: Check connection pooling. A 5-second query under load could be queue wait time for a database connection, not query execution time.

sections.title: Production debugging commands
sections.content:
-- Find slow queries: enable in postgresql.conf
-- log_min_duration_statement = 1000  (log queries > 1s)

-- pg_stat_statements (extension) — aggregate slow queries
SELECT query, calls, total_exec_time/calls as avg_ms, rows
FROM pg_stat_statements
ORDER BY total_exec_time DESC
LIMIT 10;

-- Check for stale statistics
SELECT relname, last_analyze, last_autoanalyze, n_live_tup, n_dead_tup
FROM pg_stat_user_tables
ORDER BY n_dead_tup DESC;

-- Check index usage
SELECT indexrelname, idx_scan, idx_tup_read
FROM pg_stat_user_indexes
WHERE relname = 'users'
ORDER BY idx_scan;

-- EXPLAIN ANALYZE with buffers
EXPLAIN (ANALYZE, BUFFERS)
SELECT * FROM orders WHERE user_id = 123 AND status = 'pending';

-- Fix: update statistics
ANALYZE orders;

-- Fix: clear bloat
VACUUM ANALYZE orders;

-- Check connection wait time via SQLAlchemy pool
import logging
logging.getLogger('sqlalchemy.pool').setLevel(logging.DEBUG)

seo.metaTitle: Debugging Slow PostgreSQL Queries — EXPLAIN ANALYZE, Statistics, Bloat
seo.metaDescription: Debug slow PostgreSQL queries: EXPLAIN ANALYZE comparison, stale statistics diagnosis, table bloat with VACUUM, pg_stat_statements, and connection pool investigation.

speakable_v2.hook: Dev vs prod performance gap: dev has 1000 rows, prod has 10 million — and the query plan changes when data volume changes.

beats.content: Run EXPLAIN ANALYZE on the production database. Not dev. The query plan depends on data volume and table statistics, and they're different.
Large mismatch between Plan Rows and Actual Rows means stale statistics. Run ANALYZE tablename. Check when autovacuum last ran on the table via pg_stat_user_tables.
High n_dead_tup means table bloat from unvacuumed deletes/updates. Dead tuples force sequential scans. VACUUM ANALYZE clears dead tuples and updates statistics.

speakable_v2.cap: pg_stat_statements is the production slow query log. Enable it, query it weekly, and you'll catch performance regressions before users do.
speakable_v2.followup_handoff: Follow up with autovacuum tuning for write-heavy tables, or connection wait time analysis in slow query investigation.
